candidates.summary: the height-0 key is saved before the 'validator set is nil' refusal, so a genesis refused for having no validators can never be corrected in place
candidates.failure_scenario: genesis.json carries no validators (ValidateAndComplete allows it) and the app returns none (gnoland's InitChainer returns req.Validators). ReplayBlocks saves abciResponsesKey:0 at line 353, then returns 'validator set is nil in genesis and still empty after InitChain' at line 367. The operator adds a validator to genesis.json and restarts on the same data dir: genesisApplied reads true, the persisted doc with no validators wins, InitChain runs again on it and the boot fails with the same message on every restart until the data dir is wiped. The ADR's Consequences (line 76) says a corrected genesis.json boots on the same data dir when the chain id and app hash are unchanged; this refusal is the one the diff's sweep of 'refusal must not mark genesis applied' missed. Recovery is a wipe of a data dir holding nothing committed.
candidates.verify_by: copy TestE2ERejectThenCorrectedGenesisBoots (tm2/pkg/bft/node/node_genesis_restart_test.go) with an app whose InitChain returns abci.ResponseInitChain{} and a provider that sets doc.Validators = nil on the first build and keeps them on the second; expect the second build to succeed, observe 'validator set is nil in genesis and still empty after InitChain'. Fix: move the validator-nil check above sm.SaveABCIResponses.
candidates.evidence: replay.go:353 sm.SaveABCIResponses(h.stateDB, 0, abciResponse) precedes replay.go:367 return nil, fmt.Errorf("validator set is nil in genesis and still empty after InitChain"); types/genesis.go ValidateAndComplete rejects only zero-power validators, not an empty list
